subject: ventures/window-cleaning-bid-calculator
professional: an owner-operator of a residential and storefront window-cleaning company who bids jobs weekly and knows their own loaded cost per labor hour

evidence.correctness: Ran calculateBid (node, scratch script) on 20 ground panes @1.5 min x1 side + 10 French @4 min x2 sides, travel 30 min, wage $20, burden 25%, supplies $5, other $10, overhead 15%, margin 30%, proposed $150. Recomputed by hand: pane minutes 30+80=110, +30 travel = 140 min = 2.333 h; loaded wage $25 -> labor $58.33; direct $73.33; x1.15 = $84.33 cost; /0.70 = $120.48 price; price/pane 120.48/30 = $4.016; effective rate 120.48/2.333 = $51.63/h; travel share 30/140 = 21.4%; proposed $150 margin (150-84.33)/150 = 43.8%. All matched the tool. Edge checks: negative burden rejected with a message, zero-pane group prices to $0 without crashing. Margin-on-price (not markup) is the correct convention for a quoted price.
evidence.completeness: README claims checked: per-type labor rows, travel block, loaded labor, other direct cost, overhead markup, price from margin with minimum-charge floor, recurring visits scaling, price per pane, effective hourly rate, travel share, labor split by type, walk-away price, proposed-price scoring, copy bid summary, frequency presets, opt-out usage tally, three SEO/comparison pages, llms.txt. Each has code in calc.mjs / index.html / share.mjs / proposal.mjs / usage.mjs and tests; none are stubs. The directory is NOT just README+LICENSE as first reported: it holds 20 files (calc, proposal, share, usage modules with tests, 4 HTML pages, sitemap, robots, llms.txt, VENTURE.yaml). Deployed: slug listed in platform/pages/launched.json (2026-08-26) and portfolio/usage/usage.yaml. Only README Limitations (single currency, no tax, one crew) are declared gaps, honestly stated.
evidence.verification: Ran `cd ventures/window-cleaning-bid-calculator && node --test`: 124 tests, 124 pass, 0 fail, about 0.5 s. Seeded mutation in calc.mjs: changed price = cost/(1 - margin) to cost/(1 + margin); result 122 pass, 2 fail, so the suite caught it. Reverted via git checkout (git status clean for the directory). Gap: no test recomputes an independent worked example from a source outside the author, and the page-level tests are string/structure checks, not a browser run.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs in full: pure functions, no DOM, a single validating `number` helper that throws on non-finite or below-min input, frozen presets, comments that explain why (e.g. zero minutes rejected rather than defaulted). Sides capped at 1 or 2 explicitly. Minor defects: index.html is a 51 KB single file with inline script (acceptable for a zero-dependency static tool but hard to review); proposal.mjs and share.mjs (about 38 KB together) go well beyond the README's description and are only touched on in it; `margin` for a $0 proposed price returns 0 silently; panes of 0 is accepted and prices a travel-only visit without warning.
evidence.claims: Checked: 'no network calls, no accounts' (calc/usage modules contain no fetch; usage stored only in localStorage key window-cleaning-bid-usage, per usage.mjs and usage.test.mjs); disclaimer present in README and index.html line 253 with the 'not advice, no liability' text; starting minutes labelled 'not an industry standard' in README and calc.mjs; MIT LICENSE present; live URL marisstella.app matches VENTURE.yaml and launched.json. Defects: llms.txt links all four pages to the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address (CLAUDE.md says that address now only serves redirects) rather than marisstella.app; the how-much page says the French/third-story job is 'often three to four times the labor' while the tool's own presets give 5.3x (8 vs 1.5 min) for French vs ground exterior, and no source is cited for either. The comparison page vs-servicemonster.html has its own test file, but ServiceMonster feature claims were not verified here.
evidence.fitness: Walked an operator's job: enter glass types and counts, travel minutes, wage and burden, get a price, see the walk-away number, paste the summary into a text. Works end to end and the walk-away and travel-share outputs address a real decision (matching a per-window flyer). Gaps an operator hits: no sales tax, no multi-person crew (a two-person crew halves clock time but not labor cost, only expressible by hand-editing minutes), no saving of a job or a customer list, and the owner's own unpaid time is not prompted. Usable for a first bid today; VENTURE.yaml stage is 'prototype' and all three hypotheses are untested, so no real operator has validated it.
evidence.domain: Method (labor time x loaded wage, plus direct cost, plus overhead, then margin as a share of price, with a minimum charge) matches standard service-trade estimating practice taught for window cleaning (time-based pricing with a minimum). Departures: starting minutes per pane are unsourced ballpark numbers (flagged as such, but a practitioner has no benchmark to check against); no productivity factor for billable versus non-billable hours or rework/callbacks; overhead applied only as a percent of direct cost; no seasonal, weather or cancellation loading (declared out of scope). A senior operator would accept the structure but want sourced time standards and crew size.

defects.what: llms.txt points every page link at the retired duncan-haywood.github.io address instead of https://marisstella.app/window-cleaning-bid-calculator/
Starting minutes-per-pane presets and the 'often three to four times the labor' claim have no cited source; the tool's own presets imply 5.3x for French vs ground exterior
No crew-size input: a two-person crew cannot be modelled without editing minutes by hand
A group with 0 panes is accepted and silently prices a travel-only visit
No test checks an output against a worked example from outside the author; page tests are structural

verdict: The brief's premise was wrong: this is a complete, deployed, 20-file zero-dependency tool, not an empty directory. Its arithmetic is right (a 10-input example recomputed by hand matched on price, cost, price per pane, hourly rate, travel share and proposed margin), its 124 tests pass and a seeded margin-formula mutation was caught by 2 of them, and README claims are backed by files with a proper disclaimer. It meets the bar (correctness, claims, verification all 3, median 3) and is finished. What keeps it from a 4 is the domain layer: unsourced time presets, no crew-size model, no tax, and zero real-operator validation (all three VENTURE.yaml hypotheses untested). A stale llms.txt pointing at the retired github.io address is the one concrete fix owed.
